newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine 1997 grain output forecasts.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine 1997 grain output forecasts.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE 1997 GRAIN AND PULSES OUTPUT FORECASTS
KIEV, June 17 - Ukraine's total area sown to grain (excluding maize) and pulses is estimated at 12 million hectares, with output forecast at 31-33 million tonnes (Table 1).
Taking into account maize (corn) and minor cereals, Ukraine's total grain output may reach 34-36 million tonnes.

Assuming moderate warm weather and normal precipitation, average grain yields (excluding corn) are likely to recover to 2.6-2.8 tonnes per hectare, equal to the 1991-1995 average, or 0.6-0.8 tonnes per hectare up on last year.
But if there is hot and dry weather in June and a rainy July, average grain yields may drop to 2.3-2.5 tonnes per hectare. In addition, protein and gluten contents may decline.
Winter wheat output is forecast in the range of 19.8-21.1 million tonnes, compared to 13.3 million tonnes last year.
The spring barley area is estimated to decline to 3.0 million hectares, while yields are likely to increase to 2.2-2.4 tonnes per hectare, up 0.5-0.7 tonnes on last year.
Pea output is forecast at 1.3-1.4 million tonnes. TABLE 1. UKRAINE 1997 GRAIN AND PULSES FORECAST
